supports: Comparative fossil frond diagrams including Dictyophyllum.
limitations: Comparative diagrams require species-level plate selection.

title: Early Cretaceous Gleicheniaceae and Matoniaceae from Antarctica
supports: Matonidium palmate fern-frond architecture.
limitations: Whole plant and attachment to stem are not established by detached fronds.

title: New insights into Weichselia reticulata through anatomically preserved stems
supports: Stem cortex, scales, petiole and root features of Weichselia.
limitations: Several complete growth reconstructions remain debated.

title: Fossil Plants of Fossil Butte
institution: US National Park Service, Fossil Butte
supports: Eocene Lygodium, Salvinia and Nelumbo fossil context.
limitations: Park guide is not evidence for every organ of a living reconstruction.

title: Occurrence and paleoecology of Marsilea from the Eocene Wasatch Formation
supports: Eocene water-clover foliage and paleoecology.
limitations: Fossil leaves, not a continuous complete plant.

title: Fossil Ophioglossales in the Paleocene of western North America
supports: Botrychium wightonii fertile and vegetative fragments.
limitations: Fragments are not organically connected; no complete plant is asserted.

title: The role of Hydropteris pinnata in reconstructing the cladistics of heterosporous ferns
institution: Research authors, International Journal of Plant Sciences
supports: Pinnate aquatic fern with rhizomes, roots and sporocarps.
limitations: Phylogenetic placement has been debated; organ morphology is the asset basis.

title: Geochemical support for climbing growth forms in extinct seed plants
supports: Climbing interpretations of Lyginopteris and growth-form diversity in Medullosa.
limitations: Cannot generalize one habit to all medullosans.

title: Seed Ferns laboratory
supports: Lyginopteris and medullosan fossils; seed-fern organ associations.
limitations: Some names are organ genera and must be deduplicated.

title: Glossopteris fossil leaves
supports: Glossopteris leaf fossils and tree interpretation.
limitations: Canopy architecture not established by the displayed leaves.

title: Contributions to the whole-plant reconstruction of Dicroidium
supports: Forked foliage and associations of Dicroidium-bearing seed plants.
limitations: Not all Dicroidium foliage belonged to the same trunk morphotype.

title: Seed ferns and the origin of angiosperms
supports: Caytonia cupules and Peltaspermum peltate ovulate organs.
limitations: Review; organ linkage is not equal to a known whole-tree silhouette.

title: Pachypteris
institution: Museo Etnografico e Naturalistico Val Sanagra
supports: Thick, entire-margined pinnules of Pachypteris foliage.
limitations: Leaf specimen does not prove shrub or mangrove habit.

title: Plants in the dinosaur world
institution: Stephen Hui Geological Museum, University of Hong Kong
supports: Specimens of Czekanowskia, Phoenicopsis, Ginkgo and Baiera foliage.
limitations: Use locality-specific labels cautiously; legacy broad dates are not all current.

title: Reconstructing Dicranophyllum using morphological variability
supports: Fork-leaved Dicranophyllum reconstruction based on many specimens.
limitations: Preservation affects apparent leaf spacing and branch completeness.

title: Cordaites and conifers laboratory
supports: Cordaites strap-leaf and reproductive fossil material.
limitations: Whole-tree form varies; choose a referenced reconstruction before production.

title: Palaeoecology of the late Palaeozoic Noeggerathiales
supports: Noeggerathia fossil context and reconstruction discussion.
limitations: Specific frond plate still required; not a conifer or cycad.

title: A new whole-plant species of Paratingia from the early Permian
supports: Paratingia wudensis crown of fronds and cones, differently sized pinnule rows.
limitations: Crown arrangement informed by exceptional preservation but simplified artistically.

title: Bennettitalean reproductive biology and structure
institution: The College of New Jersey, research authors
supports: Cycadeoidea reproductive structures embedded among trunk leaf bases.
limitations: Do not portray invented exposed daisy-like flowers along the trunk.

title: Reassessment of English Cycadeoidea trunks
supports: Fossil trunk structure and limits of adult leaf reconstruction.
limitations: Adult foliage is insufficiently known for confident full-plant reconstruction.

title: Anatomically preserved Williamsonia: evidence for Bennettitalean reproduction
supports: Williamsonia bockii ovulate cone with densely packed scales and terminal ovules.
limitations: Cone is known; its full parent plant is not reconstructed here.

title: A revision of Wielandiella angustifolia
supports: Branched bennettitalean shrub with associated leaves and immature cones.
limitations: Historical bisexual-flower interpretations should not be adopted uncritically.

title: Fossil cycads and Bjuvia foliage
supports: Bjuvia simplex large entire leaves and limits of whole-plant reconstruction.
limitations: Historical organ associations do not establish a complete living cycad.

title: The oldest known peltasperms with radially symmetrical ovuliferous discs
supports: Permian Peltaspermum retensorium radial seed-bearing discs.
limitations: Only reproductive-organ specimen is proposed; linked foliage is not separately counted.

title: Conifer cones from Kuehwiesenkopf
institution: Museum of Nature South Tyrol, research authors
supports: Triassic Voltzia seed cones, including attached specimens.
limitations: Cones and branches are not evidence of an exact mature tree silhouette.

title: Vegetative structure of a Lower Cretaceous conifer from Arkansas
supports: Pseudofrenelopsis parceramosa jointed shoots and reduced helical leaves.
limitations: Morphospecies boundaries require caution; no exact whole-tree architecture.

title: Sciadopitys cladodes from Eocene Baltic amber
supports: Unequivocal Eocene Sciadopitys cladodes.
limitations: Amber needles alone do not preserve a whole crown.

title: The Neogene flora of Satovcha and Sciadopitys branches
supports: Fossil Sciadopitys cf. marcodurensis leafed branches with whorled linear cladodes.
limitations: Historical cf. identification and original plates require production review.

title: Araucaria mirabilis fossil with attached cones
supports: Jurassic cone-bearing Araucaria mirabilis branch specimen.
limitations: Museum epoch label differs from some current formation datings; use Jurassic only.

title: Diversity among taxodioid conifers: Metasequoia foxii
institution: Research authors, International Journal of Plant Sciences
supports: Paleocene opposite foliage and reproductive shoots.
limitations: A fossil branch, not a generic redwood tree, is the proposed asset.

title: First South American Agathis, Eocene of Patagonia
supports: Agathis zamunerae broad leaves, shoots and reproductive organs.
limitations: Large-tree stature is inferred from living relatives; exact canopy unknown.

title: Integrating Early Cretaceous fossils into the phylogeny of living angiosperms
supports: Archaefructus morphology and alternative relationships; early water plants.
limitations: Phylogenetic and ecological interpretations are debated.

title: Montsechia, an ancient aquatic angiosperm
institution: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
supports: Montsechia shoots, leaves, paired fruits and absent roots in studied specimens.
limitations: Submerged ecology is an interpretation, not direct observation of life position.

title: Limnobiophyllum from the Oligocene of the Tibetan Plateau
supports: Limnobiophyllum pedunculatum leaves, stolons and infructescences.
limitations: Exact waterline and soft-tissue colour are not preserved.

title: Cobbania hickeyi: a floating aquatic monocot from the Late Cretaceous
institution: University of Florida repository, research authors
supports: Cobbania floating rosettes and linked vegetative structures.
limitations: Reconstruction must remain species-specific rather than generic water lettuce.

title: Monetianthus mirus, a nymphaealean flower from the Early Cretaceous of Portugal
supports: Radial fossil flower with central column and surrounding carpels.
limitations: Single coalified flower; tepal/stamen arrangement uncertain and no whole plant known.

title: Pluricarpellatia, a nymphaealean angiosperm from the Lower Cretaceous of northern Gondwana
supports: Near-complete rooted aquatic plants with peltate leaves and reproductive structures.
limitations: Precise family placement and leaf phyllotaxis remain uncertain.

title: Leaf fossils of Sabalites from the Oligocene of northern Vietnam
supports: Sabalites colaniae fan-shaped costapalmate leaves and unarmed petiole.
limitations: A leaf morphotaxon, not an identified entire living palm.

title: Florissant Fossil Plants
institution: US National Park Service, Florissant Fossil Beds
supports: Florissantia flower fossil and Eocene context.
limitations: Guide-level reference; inspect specimen image for preserved outline.

title: Dillhoffia cachensis specimen UWBM 310839
institution: Evolving Earth Foundation / Burke Museum specimen
supports: Fruit with broad funnel-shaped persistent calyx.
limitations: Unknown whole plant and family; source is a specimen catalog.

title: Reproductive and vegetative structure of Nordenskioldia
institution: Research authors, Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden
supports: Fruiting axes and vegetative associations of Nordenskioldia.
limitations: Use a reproductive specimen; total mature tree outline is not demonstrated.

title: Growth and reproductive biology of Joffrea speirsii
institution: Research authors, Canadian Journal of Botany
supports: Paleocene Joffrea shoots, leaves and reproductive structures.
limitations: Habit reconstruction is organismal synthesis, not a complete fossilized tree.

title: Palaeocarpinus from the Paleocene of Alberta
supports: Paired fruits and lobed bracts in Palaeocarpinus infructescences.
limitations: Reproductive specimen only, no additional detached-leaf asset.

title: Revision of Icacinaceae from the Early Eocene London Clay flora based on X-ray micro-CT
supports: Iodes brownii new combination, previously Biceratocarpum brownii; two-horned endocarps.
limitations: Internal microscopic anatomy is not part of the lowpoly brief.

title: Icacinaceae from the Eocene of western North America
supports: Two subapical horns and reticulate ridges of the Iodes brownii endocarp.
limitations: Published as Biceratocarpum; use later nomenclatural revision.

title: A new Trapa from the middle Miocene of Zhangpu
supports: Trapa haominiae four spreading barbed horns on fossil fruits.
limitations: Fruit form only; modern leaf rosette is not added without evidence.

title: Spirematospermum wetzleri from the Miocene of Weichang
supports: Elongate capsules and spirally marked seeds.
limitations: Family placement debated; leaves and rhizomes remain associated rather than universally attached.

title: Winged fruits of Pteleoidea from the Paleocene
supports: Winged fruit with apical notch, style and retained pedicel.
limitations: Fossil fruit morphology; entire parent plant unknown.

title: A one-billion-year-old multicellular chlorophyte
supports: Proterocladus antiquus branched multicellular thalli.
limitations: Small fossil; cellular diagnostic features require microscopy and are not asset geometry.

title: A tale of three taphonomic modes: the Ediacaran fossil Flabellophyton
supports: Flabellophyton fanlike thalli and epibenthic interpretation.
limitations: Affinity and original thickness remain uncertain; specimen representation avoids invented tissue.

title: The macroalga Bosworthia from the Cambrian Burgess Shale and Kaili biotas
institution: Research authors, Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology
supports: Bosworthia simulans revision; B. gyges moved to Walcottophycus.
limitations: Abstract verifies revision; diagnostic plates still needed for precise branching.

title: Waputikia ramosa
supports: Thick main axis and rapidly subdividing lateral branch systems.
limitations: Algal affinity tentative; basal attachment not preserved. Do not copy museum model.

title: Marpolia spissa
supports: Dense filamentous cyanobacterial tufts and Cambrian occurrence.
limitations: Not a eukaryotic plant; attachment and floating habit uncertain. No model-copy permission.

title: Protosalvinia and associated conodonts of the Upper Devonian
supports: Flattened, commonly bilobed Protosalvinia remains and Devonian occurrence.
limitations: Affinity unresolved; not a Salvinia fern or confidently reconstructed aquatic plant.

title: The green alga Chaetocladus
supports: Whorled, noncalcified dasycladalean alga.
limitations: Missing ends and species variation require a selected specimen before production.

title: New Ordovician marine macroalgae from North America
supports: Buthograptus Caulerpa-like fronds and revised Callithamnopsis branching affinity.
limitations: Abstract alone does not fix complete thallus geometry; consult species plates.

title: Complex noncalcified macroalgae from the Silurian of Cornwallis Island
institution: Journal of Paleontology / Flanders Marine Institute repository
supports: Eocladus complex branching orders and Silurian occurrence.
limitations: Reconstruction of soft thallus depth is interpretive.

title: The calcareous reef alga Halimeda: a Cretaceous genus that diversified in the Cenozoic
supports: Segmented calcified thalli and fossil record.
limitations: Generic form only; do not equate a modern species with a Cretaceous look-alike.

title: Triassic Dasycladaceae
institution: Croatian Geological Survey archive, Geoloski vjesnik
supports: Diplopora cylindrical calcified thalli and dense whorls.
limitations: Historical taxonomy; external form should be checked against original sections.

title: Aloisalthella and Clypeina: a systematic revision
supports: Clypeina marginoporella fertile whorls and distinction from Jurassic forms.
limitations: Use Eocene type-genus concept; do not reuse removed C. sulcata names.

title: The oldest fossil mushroom
supports: Cretaceous mineralized gilled mushroom cap and stalk.
limitations: Unknown colour and soft details; taxonomy naming corrected subsequently.

title: Correction: The oldest fossil mushroom
supports: Nomenclatural correction to publication of Gondwanagaricites magnificus.
limitations: Use with morphological description, not as a separate taxon.

title: Cretaceous and Eocene poroid hymenophores from Vancouver Island
supports: Quatsinoporites pore-layer fragment.
limitations: Only abraded fragment survives; full bracket shape must not be invented.

title: Fungi and fungal interactions in the Rhynie chert
institution: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
supports: Winfrenatia layered, pitted lichen-like thallus.
limitations: Symbiotic status and higher placement uncertain; microscopic partners not modeled.

title: Fossil lichens and their interpretation
institution: Museum national d'Histoire naturelle, research authors
supports: Critical review of Winfrenatia and other fossil lichen claims.
limitations: Do not present all lichen-like fossils as unambiguous modern-type lichens.

title: Paleobotany and Palynology of the Munce's Hill fossil locality
supports: Paleocene Onoclea fertile and sterile fronds documented together; later usage of Joffrea speirsiae for the Joffrea concept.
limitations: Modern colour and seasonal details are not directly preserved.

title: Onoclea sensibilis taxon profile
institution: Flora of New Zealand, Landcare Research
supports: Living analogue morphology: creeping rhizome and strongly dimorphic beaded fertile fronds.
limitations: Analogue only; paired with fossil evidence rather than used to backdate a living occurrence.

title: Vegetative and reproductive morphology of an extinct plane tree
supports: Macginitiea angustiloba narrow palmate lobes and associated reproductive organs.
limitations: Organ associations support one whole-plant concept, not multiple assets.

title: Bird's nest fungi in Baltic and Dominican amber
supports: Eocene Nidula baltica cup and internal peridioles.
limitations: Amber does not preserve original colour; cup proportions need specimen reference.

title: Cobbania corrugata: a floating aquatic monocot from the Upper Cretaceous of western North America
institution: Research authors, American Journal of Botany
supports: Contrasting leaf construction in Cobbania and Limnobiophyllum.
limitations: Genus-level comparisons do not specify every trait of the selected species.

title: Epidermal features of the floating leaves of Quereuxia angulata
supports: Compound floating rosettes, toothed leaflets and submerged divided leaves.
limitations: Family placement is not resolved; epidermal microcharacters are omitted.

title: Florissantia quilchenensis, specimen DMNH 25146
supports: Five partially fused large sepals and net venation.
limitations: Archived catalog is not updated; broad genus label avoids unsupported species-level combination.

title: Middle Cambrian Algae
supports: Original Bosworthia simulans ribbon-like branched thallus description.
limitations: Historical interpretation must be read with the 2016 taxonomic revision.

title: Fossils of the Central Lowland
supports: Buthograptus laxus fossil image USNM PAL 339997 with curved laterals.
limitations: Educational museum source; original specimen and modern revision are preferred for final geometry.

title: A new noncalcified dasycladalean alga from the Silurian of Wisconsin
supports: Lower branched hair-like whorls and upper unbranched clavate laterals.
limitations: Original paper used preoccupied Heterocladus; current name comes from 2024 revision.

title: Jimaodanus, a replacement name for the algal genus Heterocladus
supports: 2024 replacement name and diagnostic two-zone branching morphology.
limitations: Nomenclatural note; paired with the original morphological description.

title: Marchantites huolinhensis sp. nov. (Marchantiales) – A new fossil liverwort with gemma cups from the Lower Cretaceous of Inner Mongolia, China
institution: Li et al., Cretaceous Research; Lanzhou University
supports: Dichotomously branching strap-like thalli, prominent costa, and attached elliptical to circular gemma cups in Marchantites huolinhensis.
limitations: Relatively complete gametophytes; original colour and full sexual life cycle are not preserved. Gemma contents are not securely identified.

title: Corrigendum to ‘Bird's nest fungi (Nidulariales: Nidulariaceae) in Baltic and Dominican amber’ [Fungal Biol. 118/3 (2014) 325–329]
supports: Validates Nidula baltica with MycoBank 841405; corrected figures 1–2 identify the Baltic amber holotype and its cup/peridiole.
limitations: 2021 online / February 2022 issue corrigendum, paired with the 2014 description. Direct open returned 403; indexed full corrigendum text was available.
